title: When Does Test-Time Ensembling Help Large Language Models? A Budget-Matched Study of Answer-Space and Prompt-Space Diversity
description: Complete research artifacts for a budget-matched comparison of the two diversity sources available to test-time ensembling for large language models: resampling the stochastic decoder on a fixed prompt (self-consistency, answer space) versus aggregating validated semantic paraphrases (prompt space). Includes the full paper source (LaTeX), the 16-call matrix raw prediction logs for ten commercial systems across a 90-question development suite and a 119-question held-out suite, validated paraphrases with per-item NLI and embedding-similarity verdicts, the greedy-bias audits, the analysis outputs (including the held-out fragility and error-signal recomputation and the SAT-Math instruction-variant control), and the scripts (recompute_all.py, final_crosscheck.py, analyze_rq23_expand.py) that re-derive every table and statistic in the paper directly from the raw logs.
